says: Defaults: "A new project runs Opus everywhere, with high effort for threads and low effort for the conversation." The conversation is the coordinator. It decides what becomes a thread and tracks threads, while each thread opens and lands its own pull request. Coordinator and thread model and effort are set separately. The page gives no reason for the low-effort default.

"For most everyday coding and knowledge work, we recommend starting with Claude Opus 5.5." "Claude Fable 5.2 is our most capable model built for your hardest technical work." "Claude Fable 5.2 is our strongest lead agent." Sets Opus 5.5 as the everyday model and Fable 5.2 as the flagship.

Figures are in results.csv as suite AA-Briefcase. Elo on long agentic knowledge-work tasks, with a 95% interval of about 10 points either way. The Claude entries are labelled "Default Fallback". It is one of the nine evaluations inside the AA Intelligence Index, which is in the base, so it is not an independent source.

source: Anthropic, help center, Claude Fable models on your plan
says: On Max, Ultra, and premium seats: "You can use up to 50% of your weekly usage limits on Fable models at no extra cost." Fable draws on the same weekly limit as the other Claude models and uses it faster. After that, the page offers usage credits or switching to another Claude model. On Pro and standard seats Fable runs on usage credits only.

Figures are in results.csv as suite Lechmazur Writing, the six rows read. Stories scored by a panel of models, last updated 2026-11-17, 67 models. The six rows read are at high effort. Ranks: GPT-6.2 Astra 1, Fable 5.2 2, Opus 5.5 6, Gemini 4 Carbon 19, Gemini 4 Argon 27, Grok 4.7 32. The 95% intervals for Astra (4.223 to 4.379) and Fable 5.2 (3.498 to 3.636) do not overlap. Gemini 4 Neon and GPT-6.2 Sol are not listed. Read through a summarising reader. source: Hacker News, Gemini 4 Neon launch thread
says: About eight commenters say Gemini 4 writes more natural English than Claude or GPT models. Most name Argon, not Neon. These are personal impressions with no measurement, read second-hand through a research pass.

source: Artificial Analysis, Coding Agent Index v2.1
says: Figures are in results.csv as suite AA Coding Agent Index. Each model runs inside its maker's own coding tool (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI), and the score is the mean of FrontierCode-AA 2.0, Terminal-Bench 4.1, and SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA. Opus 5.5 was tested at max only. Attempts finished by a fallback model: Opus 5.5 max 77 of 966, Fable 5.2 high 51 of 966, none for Codex or Antigravity. Same operator as the AA Intelligence Index, so it stays outside the base.

Figures are in results.csv as suite Vals Terminal-Bench, the seven rows read. Every model runs in mini-swe-agent with one bash tool. The page was updated 2026-11-18 and states no effort in its table. Same operator as the Vals Index, so it stays outside the base.

source: VentureBeat, launch-week developer reports on GPT-6.2
says: Second-hand and from launch week: several named developers report GPT-6.2 Astra stopping early on long builds and say they would keep Opus 5.5 for agentic work. A separate report quotes the Codex lead saying the model changed in the three or four days before release, so early reports may describe an older build. Read through a research pass, not directly.

"Most workloads start with Claude Opus 5.5." Its comparison table lists Sonnet 5.5 for "everyday coding, agent, and enterprise workloads", so Anthropic's sources disagree, and the Claude Code default settles it. Opus 5.5 defaults to medium effort and Fable 5.2 to high. Read through a summarising reader, not the raw page.

Claude Code "defaults to Opus 5.5" on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise, and the Anthropic API. "No Fable model is the account-type default on any plan or provider." Read through a summarising reader, not the raw page.

"Choose GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday coding, writing, and work across several sources." "For demanding work across code, apps, or research, choose GPT-6.2 Astra." Sets Sol as the everyday model and Astra as the flagship. The launch notes say the same. Read through a summarising reader, not the raw page.

Hydrogen brings "speed and efficiency for everyday coding". Carbon is "Our strongest reasoning model, built for complex software engineering, multimodal knowledge work". Read through a summarising reader, not the raw page.
"While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency." Read through a summarising reader, not the raw page.

Antigravity's recommended default for "Most day-to-day development" plans with the named model and implements with Gemini 4 Hydrogen. Gemini 4 Neon is the default for new conversations. Carbon is offered on Ultra and Enterprise only. Sets Hydrogen as Google's everyday model, since it does the work. Read through a summarising reader, not the raw page.
"For everything else, including code, use Grok 4.7." xAI names no separate everyday or flagship model, so Grok 4.7 is both. Read through a summarising reader, not the raw page.
